name: Graded Motor Imagery (GMI)
founders: G. Lorimer Moseley (physiotherapist, pain neuroscientist; formerly University of South Australia, now Bradley Distinguished Professor, Adelaide University)
David S. Butler and Timothy Beames (NOI Group; commercialisation and Handbook co-authors)
founded_year_range: 2004 (first RCT, Pain 2004; earlier pilot work likely but undated); Handbook 2012, updated 2019; six Recognise apps for iOS and Android announced 2016
delivery: home programme with flash cards/mirror box
cost_summary: The protocol is published and runs within physio/OT sessions at usual rates. NOI tools: Recognise app about GBP 5.99 / AUD 9.99 per body-part app (USD price not verified). GMI Handbook AUD 50 + GST from NOI, or USD 62.95 at OPTP. GMI pack (handbook, mirror box, flash cards) AUD 139.50 + GST (2026).
conditions_claimed: fibromyalgia (single trial, with pain neuroscience education)
mechanisms: neuroplastic/learned pain (brain-generated danger signal / predictive processing)
mechanism_summary: CRPS and phantom limb pain are framed as maintained by disrupted cortical body representations: smudged or shrunken S1 maps, reduced intracortical inhibition, and impaired left/right limb recognition. These produce a mismatch between motor prediction and feedback. Pain is treated as a protective brain output, in line with the neuromatrix and Explain Pain. GMI activates premotor networks first, then motor networks, then a visual illusion of normal movement. Each step stays below the threshold that triggers protective pain, which unpairs movement from pain. The 2005 order-dependence trial is cited as support. Moseley states that the mechanism is unclear.
roots: motor imagery / mental practice in neurorehabilitation
techniques: left/right judgement (limb laterality recognition) training via the Recognise app or flash cards
explicit motor imagery of the affected limb
graded progression and regression between stages according to symptoms
small, frequent daily doses over about 6 weeks (2 weeks per stage)
tactile discrimination and graded exposure adjuncts
mainstream_notes: Widely used in CRPS and phantom-limb physiotherapy, especially in the UK and Australia; no usage surveys were found. Reported by the Burning Nights CRPS charity to be among the management options in the Royal College of Physicians (UK) CRPS guidelines, 2nd ed. 2018; the guideline text was not checked directly. Included in the Cochrane physiotherapy-for-CRPS reviews (2016, 2022) as cortically directed rehabilitation, graded very low certainty. Taught in physio curricula and NOI courses.
insurance_notes: No GMI-specific billing code. Reimbursed indirectly as part of covered physio/OT sessions (e.g., US neuromuscular re-education or therapeutic-exercise codes, NHS pain services, Australian physio). The app, cards and handbook are paid out of pocket.

key_trials.citation: Moseley GL. Graded motor imagery is effective for long-standing CRPS: a randomised controlled trial. Pain 2004;108:192-8
key_trials.design: RCT vs ongoing management, with controls crossed over at 12 weeks
key_trials.finding: About 25-point effect on the Neuropathic Pain Scale; NNT about 2 for a 50% reduction; replicated in the crossed-over controls

key_trials.citation: Moseley GL. Is successful rehabilitation of CRPS due to sustained attention to the affected limb? Pain 2005;114:54-61
key_trials.design: RCT of component order (3 arms), CRPS1 after wrist fracture
key_trials.finding: Only the laterality, imagery, mirror sequence gave the greatest reduction in pain and disability at 6 and 18 weeks; argues against a pure attention account

key_trials.citation: Moseley GL. Graded motor imagery for pathologic pain: a randomized controlled trial. Neurology 2006;67:2129-34
key_trials.design: RCT vs physical therapy and ongoing care; CRPS1 and phantom limb pain
key_trials.finding: VAS pain fell 23.4 mm vs 10.5 mm; function improved; gains maintained at 6 months

key_trials.citation: Johnson S, ..., Moseley GL, Williams AC, McCabe C, Goebel A. Using graded motor imagery for CRPS in clinical practice: failure to improve pain. Eur J Pain 2012;16:550-61
key_trials.design: Prospective clinical audit at two UK centres (not an RCT)
key_trials.finding: No improvement in pain (NRS change 0.6 and 0.2); functional gain at one centre; left/right judgement improved

key_trials.citation: Lagueux E et al. Effectiveness of tDCS as an add-on to GMI for CRPS: randomized proof of concept study. Clin J Pain 2018;34:145-54
key_trials.finding: No added benefit of tDCS; GMI+sham produced no significant pain change

key_trials.citation: Limakatso K, Madden VJ, Manie S, Parker R. Effectiveness of GMI for reducing phantom limb pain in amputees: an RCT. Physiotherapy 2020;109:65-74
key_trials.finding: Greater pain reduction at 6 weeks and 6 months, and less pain interference; no difference in quality of life

key_trials.citation: Strauss S, ..., Moseley GL, Lotze M. GMI modifies movement pain, cortical excitability and sensorimotor function in CRPS. Brain Commun 2021;3:fcab216
key_trials.design: Randomised wait-list crossover with fMRI and TMS
key_trials.finding: Movement pain fell with GMI but not while waiting; S1 hand map size, S1 activation and SICI changed in parallel

key_trials.citation: Lopez-Brull A et al. Online graded motor imagery is effective in women diagnosed with pelvic pain: an RCT. Phys Ther 2025;105:pzae164
key_trials.design: RCT, online GMI (adapted: graded exposure as stage 3) vs wait-list
key_trials.finding: Reduced pain intensity and improved sexual function in genito-pelvic pain/penetration disorder

key_trials.citation: Rierola-Fochs S et al. Graded Motor Imagery (GraMI protocol) for phantom limb pain: RCT of home-based intervention. Eur J Pain 2026;30:e70167
key_trials.design: Assessor-blinded RCT, home-based GMI vs current treatment, 9 weeks
key_trials.finding: Between-group pain difference after treatment (p=0.02) and at 12 weeks (p=0.05); no differences on secondary outcomes

key_trials.citation: Araya-Quintanilla F et al. Pain catastrophization and fear of movement as moderators in fibromyalgia: secondary analysis of an RCT. Arch Phys Med Rehabil 2026;107:383-90
key_trials.design: Secondary analysis of an RCT, GMI + therapeutic neuroscience education vs standard care
key_trials.finding: The FIQ benefit was moderated by reductions in catastrophizing and kinesiophobia; primary-outcome paper not verified here

key_trials.citation: Bowering KJ, O'Connell NE, ..., Moseley GL, Stanton TR. Effects of GMI and its components on chronic pain: systematic review and meta-analysis. J Pain 2013;14:3-13
key_trials.finding: GMI vs usual physio pooled effect size 1.06 (2 studies, n=63); no effect for left/right training alone; generally low quality

key_trials.citation: Mendez-Rebolledo G et al. Update on the effects of GMI and mirror therapy on CRPS type 1: systematic review. J Back Musculoskelet Rehabil 2017;30:441-9
key_trials.design: Systematic review (6 RCTs; 3 of GMI, 3 of mirror therapy only)
key_trials.finding: GMI and mirror therapy may improve pain, but the evidence was insufficient

key_trials.citation: Smart KM, Ferraro MC, Wand BM, O'Connell NE. Physiotherapy for pain and disability in adults with CRPS types I and II. Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2022;CD010853.pub3
key_trials.finding: All physiotherapy evidence, including cortically directed rehabilitation, graded very low certainty

key_trials.citation: Ferraro MC et al. Interventions for treating pain and disability in adults with CRPS: an overview of systematic reviews. Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2023;CD009416.pub3
key_trials.finding: No high-certainty evidence for any CRPS intervention

key_trials.citation: Limakatso K, Cashin AG, Williams S, Devonshire J, Parker R, McAuley JH. Efficacy of GMI and its components on phantom limb pain and disability: SR/MA. Can J Pain 2023;7:2188899
key_trials.finding: GMI weighted mean difference -21.3 on a 0-100 pain scale; no effect of imagined movements alone; mirror therapy vs sham no difference; very low certainty

key_trials.citation: Rios-Leon M et al. Effectiveness of motor imagery in CRPS: systematic review with meta-analysis. Pain Pract 2024;24:760-71
key_trials.design: Systematic review/meta-analysis (6 RCTs of motor imagery broadly, including GMI)
key_trials.finding: Pain SMD -1.07 immediately, -1.28 short-term, -1.18 long-term; moderate-quality evidence (downgraded for imprecision)

key_trials.citation: Williams SA, ..., Moseley GL, McAuley JH. Prescription of graded motor imagery for people with chronic pain: a scoping review. Eur J Pain 2026;30:e70220
key_trials.finding: 8 full-GMI arms, all following Moseley's 2004 protocol; component trials heterogeneous; small samples

controversy: The large effects in the founder's small single-centre trials were not replicated in a UK real-world audit (Johnson 2012, which Moseley co-authored). A GMI + sham-tDCS arm showed no pain change (Lagueux 2018). Cochrane grades the evidence very low certainty, although one independent meta-analysis rates motor imagery for CRPS as moderate quality (Rios-Leon 2024). The developer co-authored several reviews and trials and has a commercial link to the NOI Group materials. Moseley states that the mechanism is unclear, and the causal role of cortical smudging is debated. Imagined movement can provoke pain and swelling in people with chronic arm pain (Moseley 2008). Use is spreading beyond CRPS and phantom limb pain into conditions with thin evidence. MEMOIR, a definitive trial (n=204, factorial with memantine), is ongoing.

popularity.reach_estimate: About 100k cumulative patients (order-of-magnitude guess). Basis: routine use in CRPS and phantom limb pain physiotherapy across several countries for about 20 years, six paid niche apps, and a handbook in print since 2012. No published user counts.
popularity.method_notes: Qualitative estimate built from dated milestones: the founder RCTs (2004-06), the 2012 Handbook and the negative audit that year, the 2013 meta-analysis, the 2016 app launch, Cochrane inclusion (2016, 2022), and the rise in independent RCTs and meta-analyses from 2020 to 2026. The PubMed counts were re-run during the fact-check (161 exact-phrase records, 23 tagged RCTs); the earlier figure of 107 came from an unquoted query. No app download counts or Google Trends data were retrieved because the web-search budget was exhausted. Reach is an order-of-magnitude guess.
